Class KeyEvent

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tui.event.KeyEvent
All Implemented Interfaces:
Event
public final class KeyEvent extends Object implements Event
Represents a keyboard input event.

KeyEvent is associated with Bindings that determine how semantic actions (like "move up" or "quit") are mapped to key presses. Use the convenience methods like isUp(), isDown(), etc. to check if this event matches a semantic action according to the configured bindings. 

// Check semantic actions
if (event.isUp()) {
    state.moveUp();
}
if (event.isQuit()) {
    runner.quit();
}

// Or use explicit action matching
if (event.matches(Actions.MOVE_UP)) {
    state.moveUp();
}

// Or use custom action names
if (event.matches("myApp.customAction")) {
    handleCustomAction();
}

    • character

      @Deprecated public char character()
      Deprecated.
      Prefer string() for text insertion/concatenation or isChar(char) for comparisons. character() cannot represent supplementary code points.
      Returns the character for KeyCode.CHAR events as a char, or '\0' otherwise. For BMP code points (U+0000–U+FFFF) this is the exact character. For supplementary code points (emoji, rare scripts) this returns '�' (replacement character); use string() or codePoint() in those cases.
      Returns:
      the character, or '\0' for non-KeyCode.CHAR events

    • string

      public String string()
      Returns the character for KeyCode.CHAR events as a String, or an empty string otherwise. Correctly handles the full Unicode range including supplementary characters (emoji, etc.).

      Use this for text insertion, display, and string concatenation. Use codePoint() for numeric range checks.

      Returns:
      a one- or two-char String representing the Unicode character, or "" for non-KeyCode.CHAR events

    • codePoint

      public int codePoint()
      Returns the Unicode code point for KeyCode.CHAR events, or 0 otherwise. Use this when you need the numeric value for range checks or comparisons.
      Returns:
      the Unicode code point, or 0 for non-KeyCode.CHAR events
